title: Configuring Internet & SaaS for Zero Trust Browser

blocks.text: Zscaler Zero Trust Browser (formerly Zscaler Isolation) provides organizations with the capability to isolate web pages and categories of web pages, as well as isolate files downloaded from these web pages in a contained, temporary browser on the Zscaler cloud. Zero Trust Browser offers complete integration with Internet & SaaS, allowing admins to granularly define what web traffic from a user should be isolated and which policies need to be applied on the isolated traffic. To learn more, see What Is Zero Trust Browser?
To learn about configuring Zero Trust Browser for Private Access (ZPA), see About Isolation Policy.
Users must first be authenticated for any traffic and web requests to be redirected to Zero Trust Browser.
This article explains how to create a new URL filtering policy rule for Internet & SaaS to forward traffic to Zero Trust Browser.

blocks.item: Zero Trust Browser is licensed for your organization.
Admins use the isolation profiles to configure policies in Internet & SaaS. To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for Internet & SaaS and Default Isolation Profiles in Zero Trust Browser.

blocks.heading: Creating a URL Filtering Policy Rule to Isolate Web Traffic

blocks.text: Users can only enable the Isolate action in a URL policy if:

blocks.item: The protocol is HTTP, HTTPS, or both.
The HTTP method is limited to CONNECT, GET, TRACE, or HEAD.
The user agent is comprised of a minimum of one or more known browsers.

blocks.text: These parameters are automatically set after your organization enables Zero Trust Browser.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering.
Choose URL categories and any other rule Criteria.
Select a profile from the Isolation Profile drop-down menu.
Click Save to activate your changes.

blocks.text: Bandwidth Control is disabled for all traffic from the isolated browser destined to the Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS. To learn more, see About Bandwidth Control.
